text:
No, almost certainly not. With six people, microservices mostly add cost: distributed tracing, network failure modes, versioned APIs between services, per-service deploy pipelines, and data consistency problems, all paid by a team too small to absorb them. The usual benefits (independent team deploys, independent scaling) address organizational and load problems you likely don't have yet.

What to do instead: keep the monolith and make it modular. Enforce boundaries inside the codebase (Rails engines, packwerk, or clear namespaces with explicit public interfaces), so a later extraction is cheap if it's ever needed.

The case that would flip this: a specific, measured bottleneck a monolith can't solve, such as one workload (video processing, ML inference, heavy batch jobs) that needs different scaling or a different runtime. Extract that one piece as a single service, not a full decomposition. Compliance isolation or a team growing past roughly 30-50 engineers with deploy contention are the other common triggers.

If you have a concrete pain driving the question (slow deploys, test suite time, one hot endpoint), tell me what it is. Those usually have cheaper fixes than a re-architecture.
